title: Constructibility transfers to prime coefficients through an abelian sheaf isomorphism
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring. Let $r$ be a prime, $F$ a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-constructible-constructible], and $G$ a sheaf of $\operatorname{ULift}(\mathbf Z/r)$-modules on this site. If their underlying abelian sheaves are isomorphic, then $G$ is constructible. No curve, nonempty-scheme or nonzero-ring hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Theorem 03SC, second proof paragraph, passage from prime-annihilated sheaves to constructible prime-field sheaves; Definition 03RW (2),(3). Agent-expanded coefficient bookkeeping.

proof.text: Choose the finite constructible stratification of F. On each stratum its pullback is finite locally constant. The finite-module-values equivalence gives etale local constant finite module values. Forget their coefficients to obtain finite constant abelian values.

Inverse image commutes with forgetting module coefficients: compute inverse image by the left Kan extension and sheafification; the forgetful functor preserves the filtered colimits in the Kan extension and preserves sheafification. Restriction to a cover member is sectionwise. Forgetting a constant module sheaf gives its constant abelian sheaf, since constants are sheafifications of constant presheaves. Thus the given abelian isomorphism supplies finite constant abelian trivializations for the pullback of G on the same strata.

Discard empty cover members. On a nonempty member, the constant abelian value identifies with a geometric stalk; that stalk is killed by r because it comes from a prime-field module sheaf. Its finite abelian group therefore has the canonical ZMod r module structure, lifted to ULift(ZMod r). Every additive map between groups killed by r is linear: represent each scalar by an integer and use preservation of integer multiplication. Consequently the abelian trivializations and their inverses lift to module trivializations.

Each finite prime-field value is finitely generated. Apply the finite-module-values equivalence on each stratum and retain the original stratification to witness constructibility of G. For empty strata use the empty covers; for the zero ring or zero sheaf the finite values are zero.
